title: Horizontal pasting for the two-factor strict compact-support exchange
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For each scheme $T$ use $D(\mathcal T_T)$, where $\mathcal T_T$ is the category of strict inverse systems of constant $B$-module sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with the normalized functors $G_u,R_u,J_j$ [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow V,p:V\to Y)$ be a supplied compactification of a separated finite-type map $f:X\to Y$, with $j$ quasi-compact and $p$ proper [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. For arbitrary $g:Y'\to Y$ and $h:Y''\to Y'$, form the base-changed compactifications $c',c''$, ambient maps $\bar g,\bar h$ and open-side maps $g':X'\to X$, $h':X''\to X'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Put $F_c=R_pJ_j$ and similarly $F_{c'},F_{c''}$. Let $E_{p,g}:G_gR_p\to R_{p'}G_{\bar g}$ be the adjunction mate of the pullback-composition square [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and let $\beta_{j,\bar g}:G_{\bar g}J_j\cong J_{j'}G_{g'}$ be exactly the inverse open-unit transpose of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Define the actual transformation
$$e^c_g=(R_{p'}\beta_{j,\bar g})\circ(E_{p,g}J_j):G_gF_c\to F_{c'}G_{g'}.$$
For every derived strict tower $M$, with no finite-origin, boundedness or completeness restriction, these transformations are natural in $M$ and the identity-base-change transformation is the identity under the canonical identity comparisons. For $c_{g,h}:G_hG_g\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{g\circ h}$, the inverse of the canonical pullback compositor, the following is an equality of derived strict-tower transformations:
$$e^c_{g\circ h}=(F_{c''}c_{g',h'})\circ(e^{c'}_hG_{g'})\circ(G_he^c_g)\circ(c_{g,h}^{-1}F_c).$$
The open maps occurring here satisfy the specified transpose-normalized equation
$$\beta_{j,\bar g\circ\bar h}=(J_{j''}c_{g',h'})\circ(\beta_{j',\bar h}G_{g'})\circ(G_{\bar h}\beta_{j,\bar g})\circ(c_{\bar g,\bar h}^{-1}J_j).$$
Both equalities use the actual normalized adjunctions and composition identifications and hold before evaluation at any finite level; no assertion of faithfulness of derived evaluation is involved.

proof.text:
Work throughout in the specified $D(\mathcal T_T)$. Apply the pullback-square pasting statement [lem-cbc-strict-tower-pullback-square-pasting] with its three vertical maps $j,j_1,j_2$ replaced by $p,p',p''$ and its transverse maps by $g,h,\bar g,\bar h$. It identifies the outer pullback square with the paste of the two inner squares, with exactly the compositors of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to $L_1=G_p,L_2=G_{p'},L_3=G_{p''}$ and their normalized right adjoints, and to the transverse functors $G_g,G_h,G_{\bar g},G_{\bar h}$. Writing $E_g=E_{p,g}$ and $E_h=E_{p',h}$ gives
$$E_{p,g\circ h}=(R_{p''}c_{\bar g,\bar h})\circ(E_hG_{\bar g})\circ(G_hE_g)\circ(c_{g,h}^{-1}R_p).$$
This is mate pasting on the derived tower categories themselves; the cited square lemma allows arbitrary maps and imposes no boundedness or coefficient restriction.

proof.text:
Apply the first paragraph about the open comparison in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] to the cartesian squares for $j,\bar g$ and $j',\bar h$. Its inverse-unit-transpose normalization is precisely the normalization required here, and its successive-base-change assertion, written with the specified compositors, is
$$\beta_{j,\bar g\circ\bar h}=(J_{j''}c_{g',h'})\circ(\beta_{j',\bar h}G_{g'})\circ(G_{\bar h}\beta_{j,\bar g})\circ(c_{\bar g,\bar h}^{-1}J_j).$$
That assertion is for arbitrary $B$ on unbounded derived strict towers; the later finite-origin hypothesis in the cited node concerns invertibility of $\gamma_Q$, not this open comparison or its coherence.

proof.text:
Substitute the two equations just obtained into $e^c_{g\circ h}=(R_{p''}\beta_{j,\bar g\circ\bar h})(E_{p,g\circ h}J_j)$. Functoriality cancels the consecutive $R_{p''}(c_{\bar g,\bar h}^{-1}J_j)$ and $R_{p''}(c_{\bar g,\bar h}J_j)$. The remaining middle pair, at $M$, is
$$R_{p''}G_{\bar h}(\beta_{j,\bar g,M})\circ E_{h,G_{\bar g}J_jM}
=E_{h,J_{j'}G_{g'}M}\circ G_hR_{p'}(\beta_{j,\bar g,M}),$$
which is the naturality equation for $E_h$ at the morphism $\beta_{j,\bar g,M}:G_{\bar g}J_jM\to J_{j'}G_{g'}M$. Regrouping adjacent factors now gives
$$(R_{p''}J_{j''}c_{g',h'})\circ\bigl((R_{p''}\beta_{j',\bar h})(E_hJ_{j'})G_{g'}\bigr)\circ G_h\bigl((R_{p'}\beta_{j,\bar g})(E_gJ_j)\bigr)\circ(c_{g,h}^{-1}R_pJ_j).$$
By the definition of $e$ and $F$, this is exactly the required horizontal equation. All manipulations are functoriality, inverse cancellation, associativity and naturality of natural transformations.

proof.text: The mate construction [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is a natural transformation, and the open comparisons are natural by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]; their whiskerings and composite therefore give naturality of $e^c_g$ in $M$. For an identity base change, insert the canonical identity comparisons from [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. The pullback square then becomes the identity square, whose mate is the identity by clause 4 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; the open comparison is also the identity by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Thus $e^c_1$ is the composite of two identities. The argument has used only actual tower-category transformations, never evaluation, invertibility of proper exchange, or a finite-origin, boundedness or completeness hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q86-ebc496af0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all four steps of the item, all six statement dependencies and the two other cited nodes (lem-cbc-strict-tower-pullback-square-pasting, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting) in full, plus Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (l.4033) and Tag 0E47 (l.4094) and the blueprint main-20261015 proof of thm-cbc-complete-proetale. There are no new nodes, no statement change and no repair note: this is the first split of a statement-only node created by Q146. Step 1: the square-pasting lemma applies with j,j1,j2=p,p',p'' and a,b=ḡ,h̄, since ḡ≫p=p'≫g. Clause 1 of the mate-pasting lemma then gives the E_{p,gh} formula. I checked every type in the chain. Step 1 leaves implicit that whiskering a square by isomorphisms of its transverse functors whiskers its mate the same way; I checked this from the component formula of def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, and it is elementary. The report wrongly calls this 'clause 3', but the node itself does not cite clause 3. Step 2: the first open paragraph of lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus holds for arbitrary B on unbounded strict towers and gives exactly the stated β equation. Both squares are cartesian open squares, and the finite-origin hypothesis of that node, which concerns γ, is not used. Step 3: I redid the substitution, the cancellation of the c_{ḡ,h̄} factors, the naturality of E_h at β_{j,ḡ} and the regrouping into F_{c''}c∘e_hG∘G_he∘c^{-1}F; all correct. Step 4: naturality holds because e is a composite of natural transformations, and the identity law follows from mate-pasting clause 4 and the identity clause for β. Edge cases checked: identity g or h, j=id (reduces to Stacks 0E47), p=id, B=0. No duplicates among the cbc strict, pasting and exchange nodes (direct-image coherence, composition-pasting coherence, finite normalized pasting, the proper/open calculus). No SGA is cited and there are no tool_uses. No fixes.
